ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: This quarter’s missed opportunity is primarily budget-constrained, not rank-constrained: the five in-scope growth campaigns are all losing ~79–83% impression share to budget with ~98–99.9% budget utilization and 0% lost to rank at the campaign level. Brand is also meaningfully budget-limited (40% lost to budget) while delivering very strong ROAS (20.13), indicating profitable demand is being left unserved.
notable_patterns: Across the in-scope campaigns (Shopping - Apparel/Electronics/Home & Garden, Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo, Performance Max - Full Catalog), search impression share is only 17–21% while impression share lost to budget is 79–83% and budget utilization is 98.0–99.9% (with 0% lost to rank at campaign level) — classic budget cap behavior.

Brand Search - GR is also supply-limited by budget: 60% impression share with 40% lost to budget, ROAS 20.13 on €459.06 spend and 92.5 conversions, suggesting incremental brand coverage is likely still profitable.

Keyword evidence points to rank pressure within some non-brand queries despite campaign-level rank loss showing 0%: e.g., “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5) at 19% impression share with 81% lost to rank, and “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0) at 21% impression share with 79% lost to rank — suggesting pockets where bids/eligibility or query matching dynamics are limiting exposure.

Wasted coverage risk: competitor-brand zero-click terms account for 56.1% of search-term impressions (2,058 impressions) with no competitor-brand converting terms listed, implying a non-trivial share of impressions is likely low-intent noise that can be filtered to free budget for high-intent demand.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Only 18% impression share with 82% lost to budget and 99.9% budget utilization (0% lost to rank). Performance is mid-pack (ROAS 3.61 on €450.66), so scaling needs to be selective (prioritize best product groups/SKUs rather than blanket budget increases).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Add budget only if paired with tighter feed/product-group focus (exclude weak categories) so incremental spend doesn’t dilute ROAS.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Only 17% impression share with 83% lost to budget and 99.9% budget utilization (0% lost to rank). Current ROAS is the weakest of the major Shopping set (2.54 on €426.36), so the main action is reallocation/cleanup before scaling.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Reallocate budget away from low-ROAS product segments and tighten query/product coverage; scale only after ROAS stabilizes.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: 19% impression share with 81% lost to budget and 98.0% budget utilization (0% lost to rank). ROAS is 2.90 on €349.58, indicating capped volume but needing efficiency protection if budgets rise.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget incrementally but protect efficiency via product-level exclusions and/or bid/target controls on weaker items.

However, it has negative-keyword conflicts blocking an estimated 6,940 impressions (including 5,200 blocked from “free shipping promo code”), and some spend is tied to low QS terms (e.g., QS 2.5–3.5) that are likely inefficient.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Fix negative conflicts first and prune low-quality queries/keywords; then scale budget into the cleaned, higher-intent set.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: 19% impression share with 81% lost to budget and 99.9% budget utilization (0% lost to rank). ROAS is 4.47 on €134.62, but avg quality score proxy is low (4.3), implying creative/feed quality constraints may be suppressing efficiency as you scale.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget only alongside feed/asset improvements to avoid scaling a low-quality baseline.

recommendation_cards.title: Fund the capped, profitable demand first (Brand + best-performing acquisition)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Budget caps are the dominant limiter: in-scope campaigns show 79–83% impression share lost to budget with 98.0–99.9% budget utilization and 17–21% impression share. Brand Search - GR is also losing 40% to budget while producing ROAS 20.13 (€9,241.91 revenue on €459.06 spend, 92.5 conversions).
recommended_steps: Reallocate budget toward Brand Search - GR first until impression share lost to budget materially declines (start by targeting <15–20% lost to budget on brand).

Within the acquisition set, prioritize the higher-return campaigns first (e.g., Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo ROAS 4.8; Performance Max - Full Catalog ROAS 4.47) before adding to weaker Shopping areas (e.g., Shopping - Electronics ROAS 2.54).
Apply incremental budget increases in small steps (e.g., +10–20%) and hold 5–7 days between steps to confirm ROAS stability.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share lost to budget in Brand and the top 2 acquisition campaigns trending down (e.g., from ~40%/80% toward <20–30%) while maintaining ROAS (brand ~20+, acquisition ~4+).

recommendation_cards.title: Eliminate negative-keyword conflicts that are blocking your own demand
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: There are 3 negative conflicts blocking an estimated 6,940 impressions, concentrated in Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo: negative “free” blocks the keyword “free shipping promo code” (estimated 5,200 blocked impressions); “DIY” blocks “kitchen appliances clearance DIY install” (980); “returns” blocks “winter jacket sale returns policy” (760).
recommended_steps: In the negative-keyword conflicts report, change these negatives to a narrower match type or move them to a more appropriate scope so they stop blocking intended keywords (especially “free” vs “free shipping promo code”).

Where the intent is undesirable (e.g., true ‘free’ seekers), keep the negative but add a separate, explicitly targeted promo/shipping ad group/campaign with controlled bids and tailored copy to capture only qualified promo intent.
After resolving conflicts, review the newly unblocked search terms for 7 days and add surgical negatives for clearly irrelevant variants (rather than broad terms that collide with your own keywords).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impressions and conversions in Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo after unblocking (expect immediate impression lift vs. the ~6,940 blocked estimate, with CPA/ROAS not deteriorating).

recommendation_cards.title: Cut competitor-brand zero-click leakage to free budget for high-intent queries
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand zero-click terms contribute 2,058 impressions and represent 56.1% of search-term impressions from zero-click competitor terms; there are no competitor-brand terms listed that convert. This is likely consuming auctions without producing value, worsening budget pressure (79–83% lost to budget in core campaigns).
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names from the provided list (e.g., “delphi retail group”, “marathon mercantile”, “ionian goods co”, “acropolis retail quote”) as negatives in non-brand search coverage where they do not align with strategy.
If conquesting is desired, isolate it into a dedicated campaign with a hard budget cap and separate messaging so it cannot starve core non-brand demand.
Re-check the search-term feed after 3–5 days to confirm competitor-brand impression share falls and that core query volume increases under the same spend.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms dropping from 56.1% toward <10–15%, with non-brand conversion volume rising at flat spend.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix rank pockets on high-QS seasonal terms before scaling bids broadly
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Some high-quality keywords still show severe rank loss: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5) has only 19% impression share with 81% lost to rank; “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0) has 21% impression share with 79% lost to rank; even “pilot account promo code” (QS 9.5) shows 42% lost to rank. This indicates selective bid/rank constraints even though campaign-level lost-to-rank reports 0%.
recommended_steps: Segment these terms into their own tightly themed ad groups (or a dedicated seasonal ad group) and apply controlled bid uplifts specifically to the high-QS/high-intent terms showing rank loss.
Align landing pages and promo messaging to these seasonal intents to preserve QS while improving eligibility and top-of-page presence.
Run a 7–14 day test comparing impression share/top-of-page rate and conversion efficiency pre vs. post bid adjustments.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share for these specific terms moving up (e.g., 19–21% toward 30%+) and rank-lost % declining, without CPA increasing disproportionately.

recommendation_cards.title: Prune or quarantine low-QS spenders that are dragging efficiency
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Low-quality keywords with notable cost and weak outcomes include “free shipping promo code” (QS 3.5; €23.14 spend; cost/conv 46.28) and “kitchen appliances clearance” (QS 3.0; €9.12 spend; cost/conv 91.2). “deals near me today” (QS 2.5; €14.63 spend) has no conversions recorded.
recommended_steps: Move these low-QS terms into a separate ad group with stricter bids (or pause if they are not strategically required), and tighten match types to reduce broad, low-intent traffic.
Add intent-refining negatives (e.g., for “near me” local intent if you don’t serve it) and rewrite ads/LP alignment for promo-code intent if you keep it.
Reinvest freed spend into the campaigns/terms already showing strong returns (e.g., brand ROAS 20.13; non-brand ROAS 4.8).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Quality score trend (aim QS 5+ on active non-brand terms) and cost per conversion improving vs. the €46.28/€91.2 examples.

already_working: Ad creation quality is not the bottleneck: 100% of ads are rated Good or Excellent (4 Excellent, 4 Good).

You are not broadly losing auctions due to competitor dominance: average outranking share is 52.9% and your avg top-of-page rate (49.6%) exceeds competitors (42.4%) on average — pointing away from an account-wide rank crisis.
Brand performance is extremely efficient (ROAS 20.13 with 92.5 conversions), so scaling brand coverage is a high-confidence lever rather than a creative or targeting rebuild.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: You’re materially under-exposed vs. your market right as search demand and spend are rising in Greece Retail. With only 21.29% impression share and 78.7% lost to budget (0.0% lost to rank), the account is primarily capped by budget—meaning you’re not “losing”; you’re simply not entering enough auctions. External market data shows Greece Retail search spend and query demand are both growing QoQ, and the vertical benchmark impression share is higher than where you’re currently landing. Acting now captures incremental demand during a growth period; waiting risks letting competitors absorb that demand while auction pressure increases.

email_copy.banner_headline: EUR 10,754 in profit-ready demand is being left unserved
email_copy.subject: EUR 10,754 available this quarter — but the account is budget-capped
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t losing auctions because you’re outranked — it’s mostly not getting into them. With a daily budget of EUR 420, you’re hitting the ceiling and leaving profitable coverage (especially on brand) on the table.
why_now_bullets: Peers in Greece Retail typically sit around 35.0% impression share; you’re currently at 21.29% impression share — that gap is almost entirely budget-driven.
Greece Retail query demand is up 6.0% QoQ while your account is losing 78.7% of impression share to budget — you’re under-exposed right as the pool of searches expands.
Search spend is up 9.0% QoQ in-market, while your account shows 0.0% lost to rank — meaning competitors aren’t “beating” you; they’re simply showing up more often because they’re funded to.
email_copy.stat_sub: Driven by budget caps (not an account-wide rank problem)
email_copy.impact_line: The EUR 10,754 opportunity is coming from one clear pattern: your growth campaigns are running at or near full budget utilization, so coverage is being throttled before the auction even becomes a performance conversation. In other words, there’s demand you would likely take at acceptable efficiency — but the account can’t consistently access it at the current cap.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the campaign-by-campaign view of where the budget ceiling is binding hardest, so you can decide where to fund, where to clean up first, and where to hold the line.
email_copy.cards_intro: I prioritized the fixes that unlock incremental volume fastest without “turning up spend and hoping” — first by funding what’s already proving profitable, then removing self-inflicted blockers, and only then tightening rank/quality where it actually matters.
email_copy.working_intro: Before any changes: a few signals show the foundation is solid — which is why this is a funding/coverage issue, not a rebuild.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If you simply move from today’s 21.29% impression share toward the 35.0% peer benchmark, the upside isn’t abstract — it’s measurable additional reach and clicks that ladder directly into the EUR 10,754 revenue gap shown above.
email_copy.fix_title: Should I map this into a 14-day action plan for your team?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply “A” and I’ll send a tight plan built around quick budget reallocation + the first 2 cleanups, or reply “B” and I’ll send the same plan but staged to stay within the current EUR 420/day cap. If easiest, just reply “A” or “B”.
email_copy.ps: PS: The fastest win is usually unblocking demand you’re already trying to buy — once that’s fixed, every extra euro has a clearer, more predictable job to do.
